thread:
incident-bot: DETECTED: Canary pool 'canary-v13' p99 latency > 2.5s for 3 consecutive 1m windows. Auto-page to oncall.
Asha (oncall): paging received, I'm on it. Asha -> analyzing metrics now.
Sam (runtime): saw the alert too, looks correlated with the v13 tokenizer change that landed in the recent rollout.
Jordan (sre): adding context — p95 increased ~40% and p99 doubled on streaming endpoints: /v1/stream/generate.
Riley (prod-ops): traffic directed via routing rule canary-weight=10%. Rolling-forward traffic started 10:12 UTC. Metrics spike started ~10:18.
Asha (oncall): quick check: any deploys to infra around 10:15?
deploy-bot: deploy v13.1 by @Sam completed at 10:14:23 UTC (canary=10%).
Sam (runtime): yes that deploy included a tokenizer bump and a small change to kv-warmup ordering. I'm pulling logs.
Asha (oncall): customer-facing? Priya? any reports?
Priya (Customer Success): one enterprise customer reported slower streaming responses (chatty UI) ~10:20, they said p99 was ~3s on their side. No errors, just lag. Logged CS ticket #CS-9921.
Jordan (sre): reproducing locally with canary model gives similar tail stalls. I see spikes in grpc stream throughput drops and backend worker queueing.
Sam (runtime): looking at KV hit rate — prefix caching shows a cold miss surge; tokenizer change increased prefix variance. More token mismatch, less cache reuse.
Riley (prod-ops): if cache reuse down, batching efficiency drops and latency rises. Need to confirm batching stats.
Asha (oncall): Sam/Jordan run quick dashboard queries: p95/p99 for last 15m, streaming connections count, avg batch size. Paste results here.
Sam (runtime): p95=620ms (baseline ~420ms), p99=2.8s (baseline ~1.1s). avg batch size fell from 6.2 -> 3.1 for canary. stream open duration increased.
Jordan (sre): worker queue length jumped 3x on canary nodes. CPU not overloaded but per-request work spiked.
Asha (oncall): initial hypothesis: tokenizer change reduced prefix grouping -> smaller batches -> kv cache churn -> tail stalls.
Sam (runtime): agree. Quick mitigation options: 1) reduce canary weight to 0% (rollback traffic); 2) temp route canary traffic to older model variant (v12) for streaming; 3) revert tokenizer change (longer).
Riley (prod-ops): option 1 is fastest. I can flip canary-weight to 0% now. Any objections?
Priya (Customer Success): ask: if we flip to 0% will ongoing user requests fail or be routed to stable? Customers prefer stable routing.
Sam (runtime): traffic will fall back to stable v12, no failures expected.
Asha (oncall): do it. Riley go ahead and change routing. Post the command you run.
Riley (prod-ops): running: ```
# update routing
redwoodctl route set canary-v13 --weight 0 --reason "p99 spike canary v13"
```
Riley (prod-ops): applied at 10:26:03 UTC. Canary weight now 0%.
incident-bot: ACTION: Routing change recorded; rollback flag set on release v13.1.
Sam (runtime): seeing traffic shift off canary — avg batch size recovering on stable nodes. p95 trending down.
Jordan (sre): p99 dropped to 1.2s within 2m of rollback, worker queue normalized.
Asha (oncall): excellent. Marking live mitigation successful. Next: postmortem owner and immediate follow-ups. Sam to investigate tokenizer diff impact on prefix grouping and cache policy. Jordan to verify no residual downstream impacts. Riley to ensure canary is disabled for all regions. Priya to monitor CS tickets and notify affected customers.
Priya (Customer Success): notifying customers in CS-9921 thread: "We've rerouted your traffic to stable and are monitoring. Expect normal latency shortly."
Sam (runtime): quick note — create a regression test that simulates tokenization variance and verifies batching metrics before rolling future tokenizer changes. I'll submit PR for canary gating.
Jordan (sre): also suggest adding an alert for avg batch size drop >40% for any canary pool, to catch this earlier. Filing infra ticket #INF-2107.
Asha (oncall): creating incident doc and assigning postmortem: owner Sam, timeline and customer impact sections required. Severity: S2 (customer latency but no errors).
Asha (oncall): any other actions?
Riley (prod-ops): will run a quick audit to ensure no other canary pools picked up v13.1.
Sam (runtime): I'll do a bisect on tokenizer commits and try to reproduce with a synthetic workload.
Priya (Customer Success): I'll keep CS updated and close the customer loop when stable for 30m.
Asha (oncall): closing paging. Leaving thread open for follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
